## Patagonia from Tierra del Fuego to Fitz Roy and Torres del Paine

This trip through Argentina and Chile spends most of its time in Patagonia. It begins in Buenos Aires, where you have time to explore the capital and its old neighbourhoods and experience tango. Then you head far south to Ushuaia, Lakes Fagnano and Escondido, and Tierra del Fuego National Park.

From Tierra del Fuego, you travel to El Calafate for the Perito Moreno Glacier, then on to El Chaltén for two days of trekking. The shorter route leads to Laguna Capri, with views of Fitz Roy. The second hike takes a full day and climbs to Laguna de los Tres, close to the foot of the famous massif.

You then cross into Chile. Puerto Natales is your base for visiting Torres del Paine, where Patagonian steppe, glaciers and lakes surround the park's granite towers. The trip ends in Santiago de Chile, with time for the historic centre, modern neighbourhoods and the wineries of the Maipo Valley.

The landscapes change markedly as you travel through the south. In Ushuaia, you are surrounded by the Beagle Channel and the forests of Tierra del Fuego. In El Calafate, the focus shifts to ice. In El Chaltén, you explore the mountains on foot. The open plains, lakes and granite walls of Torres del Paine show you another side of Patagonia.

The journeys between stops are part of the experience. The roads cross open steppe and mountain passes and run past lakes, linking the towns across long stretches of open country. Those drives make the itinerary feel like one continuous journey through the south.
